clue.text: Measure of whiskey for Irish dancer?

definitions.meaning: a small measuring cup for spirits, holding a shot
playfully, one who dances jigs, the lively Irish folk dance

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second sense: a person who jigs.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigger is a bartender's measure for a shot of spirits, and jokingly anyone who dances a jig.

clue.text: Royalist judge, one securing death sentences?

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the card wraps round the notice

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
an obit is an obituary, sentences written on a death

explanation.surface: A monarchist judge passes capital punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacobites supported the exiled Stuart King James II and his heirs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jacobite was a supporter of the deposed Stuart kings, a royalist faction.

clue.text: Run from cave that's bugged

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letter is removed from the cave

parts.note: a grotto is a small cave
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: An insect-infested cave is fled.
explanation.definitionFit: If something got to you it irritated or upset you, an idiom for bugged.

clue.text: Take time out of school period

indicators.note: take signals removing something
out of says the letter is removed from the school's name

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: Leaving class for a break.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is an English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is a vast span of time, an extremely long period.

clue.text: Bombarded with complaints, lawyers were angry

parts.note: the bar is the collective body of barristers
raged means were furious

explanation.surface: Lawyers lose their tempers on being swamped with grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: To be barraged is to be assailed by a relentless stream, here of objections.

clue.text: US native's state overwhelmed by change

definitions.note: read as US native is, the 's a link

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means engulfed, so the state lies inside the change

parts.note: to amend is to change
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: An American Indian's homeland is swamped by upheaval.
explanation.definitionFit: Amerind is a term for an indigenous person of the Americas.

clue.text: Undergo this bumpy journey on coach

indicators.note: bumpy means jolted about, so these letters are shaken into another order

explanation.surface: Endure this jolting trip by stagecoach.
explanation.walkthrough: To ride shotgun was to sit by the driver of a stagecoach as an armed guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding shotgun means travelling beside the driver, originally on a stagecoach.

clue.text: Burroughs' hero in dull English city

parts.note: grey means dull or drab
Stoke-on-Trent is a city in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: A novelist's protagonist lives in a drab English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarzan, created by Edgar Rice Burroughs, is heir to Lord Greystoke; Stoke is a Midlands city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan, Edgar Rice Burroughs' hero, was John Clayton, Lord Greystoke.

clue.text: Fashion-conscious teenager once turned up wearing old hooded cloak

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mod was a stylish 1960s British youth
in means wearing, as in dressed in

explanation.surface: A trendy youth of yesteryear appeared in an antique hooded garment.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods were 1960s British youths devoted to sharp fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a loose hooded cloak worn with a mask at masquerades.

clue.text: Cold drink loses a little taste

indicators.note: loses a little means a small piece is dropped, here the last letter

parts.note: wine is a drink
to try is to taste, as in try a bite

explanation.surface: A chilled drink is less flavoursome.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintry weather is cold, as in winter.

clue.text: Copper notices criminal fails to make an impression

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A policeman's warnings to a crook have no effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the element whose symbol is CU; 'criminal' rearranges NOTICES into TSNOICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for having no influence or persuasive effect on someone.

clue.text: Hope dame will crumble without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters surround the next piece
crumbling breaks something apart, so the letters fall into another order

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An elderly lady's aspirations collapse when she stops fighting back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: DAME crumbles to DEAM, which wraps round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is an aspiration or cherished wish, a synonym of hope as a noun.

clue.text: From southern town, American woman takes flight

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman
a flight is a set of stairs

explanation.surface: A US woman runs off from a town in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: BROADSTAIRS is a seaside resort in Kent, in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadstairs is a coastal town in Kent, in the south of England.

clue.text: Spy AA man?

definitions.meaning: whimsically a gent marked with the letter A twice over

explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, whose patrolmen fix breakdowns; here AA is read as A doubled, and a man is a gent.
explanation.definitionFit: A double agent is a spy working for two opposing sides.

clue.text: Sound of paper boy

indicators.note: the sound of signals that a word said aloud gives the letters

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A newsboy is heard delivering.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SUN is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child, so a boy in relation to his parents.

clue.text: Question anarchist leader in the right place

indicators.note: in places the question and leader within the right-wing party's name

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative, of the political right

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Interrogating the head of an anarchist group in an appropriate location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the right place' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is the container and 'place' alone is the definition; TORQUAY is a Devon resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquay is a seaside town in Devon, south-west England, so a place.

clue.text: Catching fish? Phone home about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the call goes round the fish

parts.note: to ring is to phone
an eel is a fish
in means at home

explanation.surface: An angler calls home while landing a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catching fish?' reads as the whole definition, but the fish supplies letters; 'it' in 'about it' points back to that fish, the thing the phone call surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeling in means drawing something in on a line, catching it.

clue.text: Prom conductor returned to work in 1950s style

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so this name is read from right to left

parts.note: Sir Henry Wood founded and conducted the Proms concerts in London
op. is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A conductor of the Proms comes back to perform in a retro idiom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are London's summer classical concerts; their founder-conductor Henry Wood reversed gives DOOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Doo-wop is a vocal harmony style of pop music popular in the 1950s.

clue.text: Mule you've initially found difficult to get hold of

parts.note: a mule is a backless slipper

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter

explanation.surface: A stubborn animal proves hard to catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mule' suggests the animal, but it is a backless shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slippery cannot be gripped easily, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Film director boots one out

indicators.note: out means taken away, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: wellies are wellington boots, British rubber boots
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A director kicks someone out of the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: WELLIES is British for rubber rain boots; Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles was the American director of Citizen Kane.

clue.text: Hit man's moll?

definitions.meaning: one who strikes, the 's read as is
British slang for a promiscuous woman

explanation.definitionFit: A slapper strikes with the hand; in British slang it also means a loose woman.

clue.text: Potential slam hand at bridge? So what!

definitions.meaning: a strong deal of cards that might allow a slam bid
a dismissive retort meaning it doesn't matter

explanation.definitionFit: Sarcastically 'big deal' shrugs off importance; literally a big deal of cards may win a slam.

clue.text: With reluctance, move to cage one pet bird

indicators.note: to cage means to enclose, so the move goes round the numeral

parts.note: to budge is to shift grudgingly
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Reluctantly shifting a pet bird into its cage.
explanation.walkthrough: BUDGIE is British for a budgerigar, a parakeet.
explanation.definitionFit: A budgie, short for budgerigar, is a small parrot kept as a pet.

clue.text: Take the wind out of one's sails? Don't fret

definitions.text: Take the wind out of one's sails?
definitions.meaning: literally to leave a sailing ship without wind
an instruction to stay serene, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: To becalm is to stop a ship for lack of wind; split in two it urges composure.

clue.text: Priest occupying the living

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes up a church post.
explanation.walkthrough: A living is a church benefice; ELI was the priest in the Book of Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel.

clue.text: Go overboard when trendy group's playing inside

indicators.note: inside places the band and playing between the two letters for when

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
a band is a musical group
on means playing, as a performance under way
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: A cool group performing on board causes excess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go overboard' looks like an idiom for excess, but literally means leaving a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon ship is literally to leave it by going over the side.

clue.text: Husband's an uncouth sort, a jerk

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
oick, or oik, is British slang for a boorish person

explanation.surface: A husband is a lout and an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' reads as an insult, but it is a sharp pull; OIK is British slang for a lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoick is a sudden upward pull, a jerk.

clue.text: Approach to problem no good; bitter about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the beer goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: bitter is a British style of ale

explanation.surface: Someone finds a solution unhelpful and resents it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British draught beer, so ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is a way of looking at or tackling something, a point of approach.

clue.text: This minister's broadcast brought back into peak viewing period?

parts.note: the minister is the Prime one, so the first word of that title

indicators.note: brought back means turned round, so this word reads backwards

parts.note: to emit is to send out or broadcast

explanation.surface: A premier's TV address is shown again in the busiest evening slot.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime time is the evening slot when television audiences are largest.

clue.text: Measure of cloth to dispose of, reduced by 25%

indicators.note: reduced by signals letters being cut from the word for dispose of

parts.note: to sell is to dispose of goods
a quarter of the four letters for dispose of is one letter, here its first

explanation.surface: Fabric to sell off at a quarter discount.
explanation.walkthrough: The check names '25%' as the part removed: a quarter of four letters is one, so SELL loses its S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old unit of length used chiefly for cloth.

clue.text: Swiss cheese ruined by storeman

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A warehouse worker spoils a cheese from Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swiss cheese' is not food: Monstera is the Swiss cheese plant, named for its holey leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Monstera deliciosa is popularly called the Swiss cheese plant for its perforated leaves.

clue.text: Means of understanding viral infection found by chance?

parts.note: flu is influenza, a viral illness
a key unlocks meaning, as a key to a code

explanation.surface: Discovering the cause of a virus turns out to be luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluky describes something gained through luck rather than skill.
